To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the proposed semantic TK outperforms previous semantic TK and neural-based models, 2) the proposed neural-based similarity is better than other approaches in the literature, and 3) the proposed Siamese Network is a good approach to learn contextual word embeddings.

We introduce a new approach to learning word embeddings for semantic Tree Kernels that exploits categorical information and that our approach outperforms previous methods on question and sentiment analysis.

(1) we propose a new method that learns a similarity measure for text by using a Siamese Neural Network, (2) we show that this similarity measure can be used as a contextual embedding for tree kernels and (3) we demonstrate that the resulting semantic TK is a strong feature engineering approach for text classification.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of TKs and neural networks provides a promising direction for the development of effective semantic kernels.
